topic: Java I/O, NIO, and File Processing
learningObjectives: Identify Java classes used for reading and writing files.
Choose appropriate I/O and NIO APIs for common file-processing tasks.
Construct a safe file-processing workflow using paths, streams, and resources.

activities.title: Java I/O Class Map
activities.instruction: Explore the purpose of common Java file-processing classes.

content.concept: Java provides multiple APIs for file processing. Traditional I/O includes byte streams and character readers/writers, while NIO provides modern APIs such as Path and Files for working with files and directories.

activities.title: File Reading Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of a modern Java file-reading workflow.

content.concept: A file-reading operation commonly identifies a Path, uses a suitable Files method or stream, processes the data, and ensures resources are closed when a stream is opened.

activities.title: NIO File Workflow
activities.instruction: Arrange a safe NIO file-processing workflow.

content.concept: The NIO API centers file operations around Path and Files. A typical workflow identifies a path, verifies or accesses the file, performs the operation, processes the data, and handles possible I/O failures.

activities.title: Try-with-Resources Builder
activities.instruction: Build a safe resource-handling structure for reading a file.

content.concept: Try-with-resources automatically closes objects that implement AutoCloseable. This reduces resource leaks and makes file and stream handling safer and easier to maintain.
